NEW: 'Is StarTrack working?' self-check with a paste-ready report. Everything translated in all 8 languages.

Jellyfin 12 support from one codebase: two builds, 1.8.0.0 for 10.11 and 1.8.0.1 for 12; the catalogue picks the right one. LETTERBOXD: 'Sync everything' imports your whole profile live - every rating including films rated but never logged, every dated diary entry, then watchlist, likes and Top 4 - with never-logged films placed in the order you rated them; watchlist sync works again (Letterboxd removed the RSS feed, the page is read instead); likes, Top 4 and sign-in get through Cloudflare via an optional FlareSolverr, and back off politely with a visible note without one; imports never overwrite reviews or dates they do not carry; a known year is a matching constraint (Fall 2022 is not The Fall 2006); duplicate library copies rate the one you already rated; likes are dated by the viewing, not the import. DIARY: one viewing, one row - a playback row and its later rating merge (timezone-safe); pre-rolls and trailers under two minutes are not logged; a rating from any source fills an unrated row. RATINGS: admin choice of stars, stars+/10, or /10 everywhere an average shows (display only); IMDb ratings CSV import, auto-detected; IMDb/Yamtrack export reports what it left out. SIMKL: pull converges (#19) - any shared id matches. FIXES: tick boxes hidden by global CSS themes; poster badges fetched in one batch instead of one request per card; settings-load failures say so instead of showing everything unticked. NEW: 'Is StarTrack working?' self-check with a paste-ready report. Everything translated in all 8 languages.

Two-way Letterboxd and Serializd, plus season ratings. LETTERBOXD: push ratings, watched status, likes, your watchlist and dated diary entries back, either as a CSV that needs no password or as an hourly automatic push; an overwrite toggle decides whether a push may change a rating that already exists remotely (off by default). SERIALIZD (new): the television-only counterpart to Letterboxd. Importing needs only your username, because the diary is public - no password is stored; pushing series, season and episode ratings needs the account password, encrypted at rest. SEASONS: a whole season is now rateable alongside movies, series and episodes, with its own panel, overlay tab and Top 4 row. Season ratings are deliberately withheld from Letterboxd, Trakt, Simkl and Yamtrack, which have no concept of them. DIARY: a dated 'log a watch' control, automatic logging when playback finishes, and automatic rewatch detection. FIXES: Simkl import returned nothing at all (#19); the post-playback rating popup missed the playing item on 10.11.11 (#21); the hide-Letterboxd and hide-External-Sync toggles had no effect (#23); the TV rating panel opened but the stars could not be reached with a remote (#8); the release zip shipped without meta.json, so manual installs reported 'Not supported' (#22); the widget injection corrupted index.html on every update, leaving self-referential script tags that made browsers re-download the page as JavaScript - existing damage is now repaired automatically. In-place upgrade; no StarTrack data migration.

Media-page and TV/webOS fixes plus native-rating and BaseURL follow-ups. Issue #11/#8: keeps one canonical clickable StarTrack badge, removes legacy and attribute-stripped ghost copies, and reliably hides Jellyfin's delayed native community-rating node when replacement is enabled. Issue #8: whole-star controls are D-pad focusable/selectable with webOS-compatible focus feedback. Issue #12: adds an elevation-gated, idempotent admin backfill for existing ratings into Jellyfin's native per-user rating field. Issue #13: native item, poster, and avatar requests consistently respect Jellyfin's BaseURL sub-path. Release workflow now uses .NET 9. In-place upgrade; no StarTrack data migration.

TV/webOS accessibility, reverse-proxy sub-path support, native-rating mirror, and media-page badge fixes. TV / webOS (#8, locksoft): the media-page rating badge is now a focusable button the TV remote's D-pad can reach, is always shown on TV (dimmed when an item has no ratings yet) so there's always something to select, and shows the rating number in white (IMDb-style). The floating Rate pill is reachable by the D-pad, the post-playback rating popup is usable with a remote, and Large / Large (TV only) sizes now apply correctly on a TV. A per-device rating size (Normal / Large / Large (TV only)) can be set from My Ratings -> Preferences. Reverse-proxy sub-path (#13, LinkdxTTV): the widget and all its API calls now respect Jellyfin's BaseURL sub-path setting, so StarTrack works when Jellyfin is served under a path like /jelly behind nginx. Native rating mirror (#12, damientkyt): an optional 'Also save ratings to Jellyfin's native rating field' setting (off by default) mirrors each StarTrack rating into Jellyfin's built-in per-user rating (0.5-5 stars mapped to 0-10), so it shows in Jellyfin's own UI and works with library filters and backups; it is cleared when you remove the rating. Media-page badge (#11 / #8, khutede / locksoft): the badge no longer duplicates, goes stale, or disappears on web and iPad. In-place upgrade, no data migration.

Community bug-fixes and options (#8, #10, #11). The rating badge no longer appears two or three times on media detail pages (Jellyfin caches the page DOM; stale copies are now cleared) and the badge is clickable to open the rating panel. It drops the '(1)' count for a single rating, and a new 'Compact media-page badge' option shows just the score. The badge now sits before the IMDb / Rotten Tomatoes / community ratings so your own rating reads first. Review length is now an admin setting (default 10000; lower it, e.g. 1000) - completes #10 (thanks @debrunbaix). New 'Rating badge size' option (Normal / Large / Large on TV only) enlarges the poster badges, the floating Rate pill and the whole rating panel including the clickable stars - handy on 4K TVs; 'Large on TV only' auto-applies on TV web clients and stays normal on phone/desktop. The floating pill and badge are now reachable with a TV remote's D-pad (OK/Enter opens the panel). All new settings translated in 8 languages. Also fixes injected-widget cache-busting so plugin updates reliably reach browsers. No data migration needed.

External Rating Sync — two-way sync of your StarTrack ratings with Trakt, Simkl, and Yamtrack. Connect an account (Trakt device-code, Simkl PIN), pick One-way or Two-way, and StarTrack mirrors ratings in both directions with newer-wins conflict resolution so a fresh local edit is never clobbered by a stale remote value. Syncs automatically every 10 minutes. Also pushes watched history (marks films/episodes played on the service) and likes (Trakt Favorites + a 'StarTrack Liked' list). New one-shot Backfill button seeds the whole service from your existing library; Simkl gets a dedicated date-accuracy repair pass (rewrites watched/rated dates instead of stamping everything 'today'). Yamtrack has no public API in released builds, so StarTrack exports an IMDb-format CSV you import via Yamtrack → Import → IMDb (marked experimental). Issue #8 part 1: the poster rating badge corner is now configurable (top-right default / top-left / bottom-right / bottom-left) so it no longer collides with Jellyfin's watched checkmark. Full 8-language i18n for all new UI. No data migration needed; existing files are unchanged.

Fixes Members tab + activity feed on Jellyfin 10.11.9+ where IUserManager.Users was removed from the interface. Also dedups the unified activity feed: rating-and-diary pairs for the same item on the same day no longer surface twice (Letterboxd RSS sync writes both — only the richest variant is shown now).

New `GET /Plugins/StarTrack/StandalonePage` endpoint that returns a self-contained HTML page hosting the StarTrack overlay without the surrounding Jellyfin web shell. Auth is passed in via ?token + ?userId query params, the page seeds Jellyfin web's normal credential storage, loads widget.js, and auto-opens the My Ratings overlay. Designed for embedding the full StarTrack UI inside a WebView from a mobile app, smart-TV launcher, kiosk display, or any third-party client — same data, same REST API, just rendered without the rest of Jellyfin Web in the way. Existing Jellyfin Web users see zero behavior change.

Maintenance release with some security and privacy hardening, stricter validation around activity and import data, and safer handling for private StarTrack data. No data migration needed; existing files are unchanged.

Major release. Members tab + profile pages with Letterboxd-style stats (histogram, genres, directors, actors, decades, hours watched, calendar heatmap, on-this-day, most rewatched, year cards). Follow graph with followers/following lists. Activity feed across people you follow or everyone. Compare profile UI: taste-similarity score, side-by-side rating distributions, biggest disagreements, and films you both loved. Dedicated Reviews tab. Privacy toggles (hide from members / follower count / following / stats / recent activity) and optional private lists. Diary now shows a clearer rewatch pill with stars right-aligned. Significant performance work — profile and stats endpoints serve cached data instantly while rebuilding fresh data in the background, plus a server-wide item/people cache so heavy users are no longer slow to load. Includes a security pass across endpoints. No data migration needed; existing files are unchanged.

Bug fix: the Rate pill and My Ratings sidebar entry were showing up on Jellyfin's login page and server-picker. New isPreAuthPage() check: hides on any URL matching /login.html, #!/login, #!/addserver, #!/selectserver, #!/wizard, /quickconnect, or when document.body has class 'loginPage', or when no user is logged in yet (no getUserId()). Physically removes the sidebar link + hides the pill so nothing leaks pre-auth.

Actual fix for Letterboxd likes not syncing (v1.4.3 + v1.4.4 were wrong). Root cause: the RSS parser was looking for <letterboxd:liked> but the real field name in Letterboxd RSS is <letterboxd:memberLike> (values 'Yes'/'No'). So entry.Liked was always false and the like catch-up loop found nothing. Verified against davidehrlich's public RSS feed, which ships <letterboxd:memberLike>No</letterboxd:memberLike> on every entry. Parser now reads memberLike (with liked as a forward-compat fallback) so rated+liked entries finally mirror their like into StarTrack. No other code changes required — the 1.4.4 catch-up pass was correct, it just never had any data to work with.

Follow-up to 1.4.3 likes-sync fix: also catch up likes on PREVIOUSLY-SYNCED rated entries. Root cause: SyncRssAsync uses LastSyncedGuid to break out of the walk once it hits a previously-seen entry. So if you rate a film on Monday, sync on Monday (rating + diary come through), then like it on Tuesday and sync on Tuesday — the Monday-rated entry is skipped because its GUID IS the last-synced-guid, and the like is never mirrored. Fixed by adding a separate likes-only pass after the main loop that walks every RSS entry (ignores LastSyncedGuid) and calls AddLikeAsync for any rated+liked entry. AddLikeAsync is idempotent so re-syncing is free. Works for likes added days or weeks after the original rating.

Bug fix from community feedback: when a user rated AND liked a film on Letterboxd, the rating and diary entry synced to StarTrack but the like didn't. Root cause: the RSS parser never read the <letterboxd:liked> field (present on every RSS entry that the user has liked), and the HTML likes scraper is a fragile fallback that doesn't always catch new likes. Now the RSS parser extracts the liked flag and the sync loop calls AddLikeAsync for any rated-and-liked entry. AddLikeAsync is idempotent so re-syncing doesn't create duplicates. The HTML scrape still runs afterwards for pure unrated likes.

Two bug fixes from community feedback against 1.4.1. (1) FIXED: Top 4 favourites row still appeared on Watchlist / Liked / Diary / Reviews / For you / Lists despite the 1.4.1 fix — root cause was a CSS `display:flex!important` rule on `.ir-ov-favs` that beat the inline `style.display='none'` hide. Now toggled via a class with its own `!important` rule. (2) FIXED: Reviews feed ignored every topbar control — type tabs, search box, star filter, sort dropdown all had no effect. `renderReviewsView` now applies the same filter pipeline as the other views (type tab via metadata.type / isAnime, search query against item name, star filter against rating, ten-way sort by date / year / rating / runtime). Also shows a 'N reviews' count in the topbar pill and an empty-state message when filters match nothing.

Three community-requested admin settings. (1) COMMUNITY RECENT MODE — new admin toggle makes the floating Recent pill show recent ratings from EVERY user on the server (with their name next to each entry) instead of only the current user's. (2) HIDE OVERLAY VIEWS — admin can now hide any of Watchlist / Liked / Diary / Reviews / For you / Lists from every user on the server. The Media (films) view is always available. Previously the full seven-view menu was forced on everyone. (3) Top 4 favourites row is now correctly hidden on non-Media views (Watchlist/Liked/Diary/Reviews/For you/Lists) — it was leaking into other views in 1.4.0 where it made no sense. Fixes 'pin a film' / 'pin a series' label not reflecting the active type tab on non-Media views — moot now that the row is only on Media.

Big feature release. (1) 8-LANGUAGE I18N — en, fr, es, de, it, pt, zh, ja. Widget pill + rating panel + My Ratings overlay + admin config page all translate. Translation bundles embedded via WithCulture=false so they survive the satellite-assembly collapse. DOM scrub uses a canonical-English baseline so switching fr→de→en→ja all work without a reload. (2) USER LANGUAGE PICKER — globe button in the rating panel lets each user pick their own language, persisted per-browser in localStorage. (3) USER PREFERENCES MODAL — gear Preferences button in the My Ratings overlay opens a per-user settings dialog: language, hide the floating Rate pill, hide the post-playback rating popup. (4) ADMIN SETTINGS — Dashboard → Plugins → StarTrack now has a full settings form: default language, hide Recent / Letterboxd / Rate-pill floating buttons system-wide, replace native ratings on media detail pages, replace Media Bar plugin ratings, overlay ratings on library posters, post-playback rating popup. (5) POSTER RATING BADGES — gold star badge in the top-right corner of every library card whose item has a StarTrack rating. (6) MEDIA DETAIL RATING SWAP — replaces Jellyfin's native community rating on movie/series detail pages with the StarTrack average + rater count. (7) MEDIA BAR PLUGIN SWAP — if the Media Bar plugin is installed, its rating pills are replaced with StarTrack's average. (8) POST-PLAYBACK RATING POPUP — when a movie or episode finishes, a small prompt asks the user to rate (once per item, skipped if already rated). (9) MY RATINGS POPUP SIZING FIX — works correctly on non-default Jellyfin themes now (width/height:100dvh, transform:none, body lock). ARCHITECTURAL NOTE: Jellyfin strips inline <script> tags from plugin config pages on SPA navigation, so all admin-page JS logic now lives in widget.js which is injected globally via the ScriptInjectionMiddleware.

Films view renamed to 'Media' to reflect the fact that it already covers movies, TV shows, and episodes — the label just implied it was movies-only. New Anime type tab sits alongside All / Movies / TV Shows / Episodes. Anime isn't a real Jellyfin type — the detection is genre/tag based: any item whose Genres or Tags field contains the word 'anime' (case-insensitive) is treated as anime, regardless of whether its underlying type is Movie, Series, or Episode. The metadata batch now pulls Genres + Tags alongside the existing fields, and each item carries an isAnime flag through the hydration pipeline. Top 4 Anime row appears when the Anime tab is active, pulling any pinned favorites that are anime regardless of which underlying-type bucket they live in.

Hygiene pass from a full-plugin audit. All five JSON repositories (ratings, user interactions, diary, lists, Letterboxd settings) now write atomically: serialize to '<file>.tmp' then 'File.Move(..., overwrite: true)'. Previously 'File.WriteAllTextAsync' was used directly on the live file, so a process kill or power loss mid-write would truncate or corrupt the JSON and wipe every rating, review, watchlist entry, diary entry or list on that file. File.Move is atomic on NTFS when source and target are on the same volume, which they are because the temp file is a sibling. No behaviour changes, no new features — just making the persistence layer safe against crashes.

User picker on Everyone's watchlist + full README rewrite. New: when viewing the everyone's-watchlist scope, a user dropdown appears next to the scope buttons letting you filter the aggregated view to a single user (e.g. show only Adam's watchlist). The dropdown is populated from whichever users actually appear in the aggregated data, sorted alphabetically. README rewritten end-to-end to reflect every feature added across the 1.0.x → 1.3.x line: ratings + reviews, full Letterboxd-parity views (Films, Watchlist, Liked, Diary with rewatches, Reviews feed, For You recs, collaborative Lists), per-type Top 4 favourites, full Letterboxd integration (ZIP/CSV import, RSS sync, likes scrape, favorites scrape, CSV export), search + discrete star filter, mobile-responsive UI, client-side metadata cache, and a clear AI-assisted disclosure at the bottom.

Seven fixes and features. (1) FIXED: Top 4 favorites strip occasionally bled into Watchlist/Liked/Diary/Reviews/Lists views — root cause was a stale fetch callback re-showing the row after the user switched views. Added a defensive view check inside the callback. (2) FIXED: list detail page had a horizontal scrollbar from overflowing content; container now word-wraps and respects max-width. (3) FIXED: clicking a film card popped Jellyfin's nav drawer because window.location.hash was being set while the overlay was still closing. New navigateToItem() helper closes the overlay, blurs focus, defers 60ms, and uses Jellyfin's appRouter.show() / Emby.Page.show() before falling back to a hash assignment. (4) FIXED: mobile Letterboxd panel inputs overflowed the panel border — added box-sizing: border-box on every child of .ir-ov-lb-row in the mobile media query. (5) FIXED: For-you recommendations excluded TV series — query now includes both BaseItemKind.Movie and BaseItemKind.Series, and the path-exists check accepts Directory.Exists too (Series have folder paths, not file paths). (6) NEW: delete-list buttons. The list detail page shows a 'Delete list' button to the owner; the list cards in the index show an X icon on hover (also owner-only). Confirmation prompt before deletion. (7) NEW: 'Everyone's watchlist' view inside the Watchlist tab — toggle pills at the top let you flip between 'My watchlist' and a server-wide aggregated view sorted by how many users want each title. New endpoint GET /Plugins/StarTrack/EveryonesWatchlist returns each item with the list of users who have it. Cards show 'N users: zack, adam, mum +X' on the everyone view.

Six fixes and features. (1) FIXED: rewatches via Sync now didn't show up in diary — SyncRssAsync only wrote to ratings, not the diary store. Now writes a diary entry for every imported RSS rating with the rewatch flag parsed from the letterboxd:rewatch RSS field. Re-syncing dedupes on (itemId, day). (2) Top 4 favorites is now bound to the active type tab — clicking 'Movies' shows Top 4 Movies, 'TV Shows' shows Top 4 Series, 'Episodes' shows Top 4 Episodes. The 'All' tab still shows all populated rows. Type-tab clicks now refresh the favorites strip too. (3) Create-list modal — replaces the cascade of window.prompt() calls with a proper modal: name field, description textarea, collaborative checkbox, focus + Enter to confirm, animated backdrop, success toast. (4) Reviews feed tab — new ✍ Reviews view in the topbar shows every rating with a non-empty review across the whole server, rendered as a vertical feed with poster, film name, reviewer, star bar, date, and the review text in an italic blockquote-style block. (5) Mobile responsive CSS — full @media (max-width: 768px) and (max-width: 380px) overhaul. The topbar wraps cleanly, search/filter become full-width, view tabs become horizontally scrollable, the favorites grid drops to 2 columns, the Letterboxd panel buttons stack instead of overflowing, modals fit within the viewport, and hover-actions become always-visible since touch devices have no hover state. (6) Top 4 episodes pin row added (was Movies + Series only).

Big bug-fix bundle from log analysis. (1) FIXED: likes.csv was never importing because Letterboxd packs it inside likes/films.csv (a subfolder), not at the ZIP root. The CSV finder now matches both bare filename and full path. (2) FIXED: Letterboxd 403 on watchlist RSS and likes scrape — the default .NET HttpClient User-Agent is blocked by Letterboxd's anti-bot. Now sends a real Chrome 124 UA + proper Accept headers, so all three Letterboxd fetches (favorites scrape, watchlist RSS, likes scrape) work consistently. (3) FIXED: import counters were lying — 'skipped' lumped 'film not in library' with 'already on watchlist'. Now logged separately as alreadyOnWatchlist + notInLibrary so you can see what's actually happening. (4) STAR FILTER is now discrete — All ratings, 5★, 4.5★, 4★, 3.5★, ... down to 0.5★ — match exactly one star value rather than 'and up' ranges. (5) DIARY entries now show a real visual 5-star bar (filled / half / empty glyphs) instead of a number, exactly as requested. Half stars use a CSS clip-path overlay. (6) ADD-TO-LIST now opens a proper modal dialog — clickable list rows with film counts, inline 'create new list' input, focus + Enter to confirm, success toast on add. No more window.prompt. (7) TOP 4 is now per-type — Top 4 Movies, Top 4 Series, Top 4 Episodes. The Movies row always shows; the Series and Episode rows only appear when you've pinned at least one item of that type. Pin cap raised from 4 to 12 (4 of each type). When you click the star-pin button on a series, it goes into the Series row, not Movies.

Polish + bug-fix bundle on top of 1.3.0. (1) FIXED: 'Newest rated' sort returning random order — root cause was the Letterboxd CSV importer setting RatedAt to DateTime.UtcNow for every row, so every imported rating clustered at the same instant and the sort comparator couldn't distinguish them. Now parses the Date column from ratings.csv and uses the original Letterboxd timestamp. The sort comparator is also defensive against null/NaN dates and falls back to alphabetical title sort on ties. (2) FIXED: Sync now didn't pull likes — Letterboxd has no public RSS feed for likes, so the new SyncLikesScrapeAsync fetches the /username/likes/films/ HTML page and parses the poster grid via regex. Wired into SyncRssAsync alongside the existing watchlist sync. One Sync now click now gets ratings + watchlist + likes. (3) NEW: hover actions on every grid card — pin to favorites, add to a list. The card highlights as you hover and the actions slide in from the top-right. Add-to-list opens a numbered prompt of your existing lists with an option to create a new one. (4) NEW: X button on Top 4 favorite slots — hover any filled slot to reveal a red × that removes the film from the slot. (5) NEW: star tier badges with color differentiation — 4.5+ gets bright gold + glow, 4-4.4 gold, 3-3.9 silver-blue, 2-2.9 bronze, below 2 muted red. Makes the grid scannable at a glance. Safe in-place upgrade from 1.3.0; no schema changes.

Polish + major features. (1) DIARY now has its own storage with rewatch support — import diary.csv from the Letterboxd ZIP and rewatches of the same film show up as separate entries grouped by month, with dates and review text visible per row. New endpoints: GET /MyDiary, POST /Diary, DELETE /Diary/{id}. (2) STAR FILTER dropdown in the topbar — filter any view by rating range (4.5+, 4+, 3+, 2+, below 3). (3) RECOMMENDATIONS reshuffle — big red button at the top of the For you view that rerolls 30 picks from a 60-candidate pool, so different films show up every click. (4) EXPORT CSV button in the topbar — downloads your ratings as a Letterboxd-compatible ratings.csv (Date, Name, Year, Rating) for backup, migration, or round-tripping back to Letterboxd. New GET /ExportCsv endpoint. (5) SYNC NOW now also pulls your Letterboxd watchlist RSS feed — one click syncs ratings AND watchlist additions. (6) IMPORT TOP 4 button in the Letterboxd panel — scrapes your public Letterboxd profile page for the 'favourite films' section and sets them as StarTrack favorites. (7) TOP 4 FAVORITES row is now always visible on the Films view with 4 numbered placeholder slots when empty, so the feature is discoverable. Enhanced hint text. (8) COLLABORATIVE LISTS — new Lists view in the overlay. Create a list, add films, and other users on the server can also contribute to collaborative lists. New endpoints: GET /Lists, POST /Lists, DELETE /Lists/{id}, POST /Lists/{id}/Items, DELETE /Lists/{id}/Items/{itemId}. (9) PERFORMANCE — client-side metadata cache means switching between views is instant after the first load. No more re-fetching the same Jellyfin items every tab click. New storage files: diary.json, lists.json. Existing ratings.json and user_interactions.json unchanged. Safe in-place upgrade from 1.2.0.

Big feature release. (1) WATCHLIST — new bookmark button on the rating pill + Watchlist view in the overlay. Also imported from Letterboxd's watchlist.csv automatically when you drop the export ZIP in. (2) LIKED FILMS — a heart toggle on the rating pill separate from star rating (Letterboxd-style). Imports from likes.csv. New Liked view in the overlay. (3) DIARY VIEW — chronological list of everything you've rated, forced newest-first, with dates and reviews visible per card. (4) TOP 4 FAVORITES — pin up to 4 films as your profile favorites with a dedicated row at the top of the Films view. Fifth pin prompts to replace the oldest. (5) RECOMMENDATIONS — new 'For you' tab that computes your genre preferences from your existing ratings (weighted by star count) and surfaces unrated films in your top-3 genres, sorted by community rating. Uses Jellyfin's existing library query, no external calls. (6) SEARCH — live search input in the overlay topbar, filters the active view by title substring with a 150ms debounce. All six features work together in a single unified My Ratings overlay with view tabs, type sub-filters, sort dropdown, and search. New endpoints: /Interactions/{itemId}, /MyWatchlist, /Watchlist/{itemId}, /MyLikes, /Likes/{itemId}, /MyFavorites, /Recommendations. New storage file at /InternalRating/user_interactions.json. All existing endpoints and ratings.json data unchanged — safe in-place upgrade from 1.1.6.

Zombie library item filter + dead ratings cleanup. User reported that after a hard drive failure, Jellyfin kept zombie DB entries for movies whose files no longer exist on disk — the rating pill matched to these zombies, so imports succeeded but the My Ratings grid showed broken thumbnails for unplayable items. Two fixes: (1) BuildMovieLookup now skips items whose Path doesn't resolve via File.Exists, so new imports only ever land on real files. Diagnose UI shows how many zombies were filtered. Network mounts that are temporarily unreachable are still treated as alive so a momentary blip doesn't wipe the user's library. (2) New 🗑 Clean dead ratings button in the overlay Letterboxd panel iterates every existing StarTrack rating, checks whether the referenced item still exists and has a living path, and deletes any that don't. Returns a count of rows + items removed. Confirmation prompt before running. New POST /Plugins/StarTrack/Letterboxd/Cleanup endpoint exposes the same operation.

THE fix for the 113 ambiguous imports. Real-world diagnostic from a 2,651-movie library showed that 1,065 movies shared a normalized title with at least one other movie (mostly duplicate 4K/HD copies across libraries, plus genuine franchise collisions like 'King Kong' 1933/1976/2005). The old matcher bailed with 'ambiguous' whenever the year disambiguation didn't pick a unique winner, so 113 out of 154 CSV rows silently dropped. New matcher ALWAYS picks a winner: exact year → closest year → oldest year → first candidate. Multiple library copies of the same film now always match. Also fixes the Diagnose button showing 'Library query returned undefined movies' — Jellyfin's default JSON serializer isn't camelCase, so the client's d.libraryMovieCount was always undefined. Fixed by adding explicit JsonPropertyName attrs on every DTO property forcing camelCase, plus a defensive camelCase/PascalCase accessor in the client. Diagnose UI now also shows unique-normalized-title count so you can see how much collision you have upfront.

Diagnostic tooling for Letterboxd sync. New 🔍 Diagnose button in the My Ratings overlay runs the same library query the matcher uses and shows you the total movie count, whether the fallback query was needed, and the first 20 movies with both their original and normalized titles — so you can see at a glance whether StarTrack can see your library and how your titles are being normalized. New GET /Plugins/StarTrack/Letterboxd/Diagnose endpoint returns this data as JSON for scripting. Also adds INFO-level request logs at the top of the Import and SyncNow endpoints so you can verify in the Jellyfin server log that the request is actually reaching the plugin.

Letterboxd matcher rewritten. Previous versions ran a separate library query per CSV row with InternalItemsQuery.Years as a filter, which silently returned 0 results on some Jellyfin setups and was also slow. New approach: fetch every Movie from the library ONCE per import, build an in-memory dictionary keyed by normalized title, then match everything against that dictionary. Much faster and handles year drift cleanly (exact year → ±1 year fallback). Also adds a library fallback query that re-fetches without type filter and filters in-memory by GetBaseItemKind — covers the case where IncludeItemTypes returns nothing. The import result now includes libraryMovieCount, and the status line in both the overlay and the small widget shows it next to the import summary so you can immediately see whether the library query is working at all. Every unmatched title is logged at Debug level with its normalized form so you can diagnose matching gaps from the Jellyfin server logs.

Three Letterboxd UX fixes reported against 1.1.1. (1) Letterboxd settings are now also available from the big 'My Ratings' full-page overlay — new gold '⚙ Letterboxd' button next to Close opens an inline settings panel with the username field, auto-sync toggle, Save / Sync now buttons, and file upload, so you don't have to dig into the small rating pill to configure sync. (2) CSV import now accepts the Letterboxd export ZIP directly — just drag in the .zip you downloaded from letterboxd.com, the server extracts ratings.csv (with diary.csv as a fallback) automatically. No more manually extracting the archive. (3) Title matching is far more forgiving: strips diacritics so 'Amélie' matches 'Amelie', normalizes leading/trailing 'The/A/An' so 'The Matrix' matches 'Matrix, The', and treats apostrophes / colons / Unicode dashes / curly quotes / ampersands as word separators. Sync and import also surface a list of unmatched titles under the status line so you can see exactly which films from Letterboxd weren't found in your library. No schema/endpoint changes, safe in-place upgrade from 1.1.1.

versions.changelog:
# v2.6.4

A larger follow-up to v2.6.3 built almost entirely from contributor PRs: app passwords get safer and work for SSO and passkey accounts, admins can be alerted by email or Telegram, the setup page fits SSO-only users, and the dependency pins that held since the spring are finally lifted after live re-verification. Drop-in from any 2.5.x or 2.6.x, with no config or data migration.

## App passwords

- **An app password no longer signs in to the Jellyfin web interface** *(#249, by @camarigor; #244).* App passwords are for native apps; accepting one in a browser session defeats the point. A native client (Symfonium, Findroid, Seerr, and the like) still uses them exactly as before.
- **SSO and passkey accounts can create app passwords** *(#252/#248, by @camarigor).* Accounts that sign in through an identity provider or with a passkey, and so have no TOTP, were stuck with no way to make an app password for a native client. A linked provider (or a passkey) now satisfies the step-up that creating one requires.

## Sign-in and setup

- **Hide the plugin's 2FA setup from SSO users** *(#250/#247, by @camarigor).* An opt-in admin setting: a non-admin who signs in through a linked provider sees that the provider handles sign-in instead of the plugin's own TOTP/passkey enrolment. Administrators keep the full page.
- **A clearer authenticator rotation flow** *(#255/#254, by @camarigor).* The setup page shows the rotate card, and your old authenticator keeps working until the new one is confirmed.
- **OIDC errors tell a refused sign-in apart from an expired code** *(#234/#64, by @camarigor).*
- **The login page works behind an access proxy** *(#253/#251, by @camarigor):* the plugin's own requests now carry the page's cookies.
- **The admin Users tab saves an edited email reliably** through the step-up prompt *(#264/#263, by @camarigor).*

## Notifications and detection

- **Admin alert emails, and Telegram as a channel** *(#261/#259, by @camarigor).* Security events (suspicious sign-in, emergency lockout) can now notify admins by email or Telegram.
- **Turn suspicious-login detection off** *(#260/#258, by @camarigor),* and leave impossible-travel out of the security score when geo checks run elsewhere.

## Correctness

- **Sign-in no longer saves a stale copy of the user record** *(#257/#256, by @camarigor),* which could drop a concurrent change made during sign-in.

## Dependencies

- **The QuestPDF and IdentityModel pins are lifted** *(#262, by @camarigor).* `Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens` / `System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt` move to 8.23.0 and QuestPDF to 2026.9.1, after re-verifying a live OIDC sign-in and the recovery-code PDF on both the 10.11 and 12 builds. The spring OIDC regression turned out to be a missing bundled assembly, shipped since v2.6.2, not the library. Fido2 moves to 4.2.0 and MailKit to 4.18.1. The Jellyfin runtime references stay pinned.

## Upgrade notes

In-place upgrade from any 2.5.x or 2.6.x, with no schema or configuration migration. Both the 10.11 (.NET 9) and 12 (.NET 10) packages are published and your server selects the right one automatically. Sigstore-signed and SLSA build-provenance attested.

# v2.6.3

A safety release on top of v2.6.2: uninstalling, disabling, or losing the plugin no longer locks out the accounts that used it. Drop-in from any 2.5.x or 2.6.x, with no config or data migration.

## Accounts are handed back to Jellyfin when the plugin goes away

*(Fixes #232, seen in #213, by @camarigor.)*

Signing in with a passkey, creating an app password, or using the OIDC bridge moves an account onto the plugin's own sign-in provider, and nothing moved it back. So once the plugin was uninstalled, disabled, or failed to load, Jellyfin refused every sign-in for those accounts, administrators included.

The plugin now hands those accounts back to Jellyfin's own authentication provider when it is uninstalled or disabled, and takes them back the next time it starts (so an app password created before the uninstall works again after a reinstall). Concretely:

- **Uninstall** moves every account on the plugin's provider back to the provider the plugin was delegating password checks to (Jellyfin's default on a stock server), before Jellyfin removes the plugin.
- **Disable** does the same, through a filter that runs after Jellyfin disables the plugin.
- **Reinstall / re-enable** then restores those accounts to the plugin on the next start, each only while it is still on the handed-back provider.

The hand-back only ever runs on an administrator's own uninstall or disable, and only moves accounts that are actually on the plugin's provider; while the plugin is running, nothing changes.

## Recovery when the plugin cannot load

No code can run for a plugin folder that was deleted or a build that will not load, so the README now documents the ways out: re-enable and restart, save the account's profile page (which moves it to the default provider), or the two-line `sqlite3` fix with Jellyfin stopped.

## Upgrade notes

In-place upgrade from any 2.5.x or 2.6.x, with no schema or configuration migration. The only new on-disk state is a short-lived `handed-back.json` that exists between a hand-back and the next start. Both the 10.11 (.NET 9) and 12 (.NET 10) packages are published and your server selects the right one automatically. Sigstore-signed and SLSA build-provenance attested.

# v2.6.1

A focused fix release on top of v2.6.0: OIDC sign-in now hands off to the 2FA prompt correctly when a user has both SSO and plugin TOTP, and a native-library crash that could core-dump the whole Jellyfin process is gone. Drop-in from any 2.5.x or 2.6.0, with no config or data migration.

## OIDC sign-in reaches the 2FA prompt instead of erroring

*(Fixes #204, by @Faffu.)*

If a user signed in with OIDC/SSO **and** also had plugin TOTP enabled, the sign-in stopped on the callback page with **"Sign-in could not be completed. Error: HTTP 401"**. That 401 was actually the expected `TwoFactorRequired` response with a challenge token, but the bridge page treated any 401 as a terminal failure and never opened the TOTP page.

Both sign-in bridges (the browser callback and the in-app webview) now recognise a `TwoFactorRequired` response and continue to the existing 2FA challenge, then complete sign-in once the code is accepted. A wrong code is still rejected, an ordinary 401 is still an authentication failure, and credentials are not stored before the second factor is completed. The challenge redirect is built from the server's own base path, never from anything in the response.

## No more `libsodium` core dumps

*(Fixes #203, reported by @bluej007.)*

On some hosts (seen on the linuxserver.io image on Jellyfin 12) the Jellyfin process could randomly core-dump while browsing the dashboard, with the crash inside the dynamic linker loading `libsodium.so`.

The cause was the recovery-code PDF service eagerly loading `libsodium.so` as if it were a QuestPDF dependency. It is not: `libsodium` belongs to the passkey code (NSec), and loading it late from the PDF path meant even servers that never use passkeys pulled it in, where a late load of that library can crash glibc's loader outright. The PDF service now loads only its real native dependencies; `libsodium` is loaded on demand only when a passkey is actually used, so passkeys are unaffected and everyone else stops crashing.

## Upgrade notes

# v2.6.0

**Jellyfin 12 is supported.** This release ships a second build so the plugin loads and runs on Jellyfin 12 (which moved to .NET 10), while the existing build keeps serving Jellyfin 10.11.x exactly as before. Both live in the one plugin catalog under the same entry, so your server downloads the build that matches its version: there is nothing to pick and existing installs update themselves. It also fixes the admin step-up prompt on the settings save path and the OIDC provider form, and makes the GeoIP diagnostics finally explain themselves. Drop-in from any 2.5.x, with no config or data migration.

## Jellyfin 12 support, without dropping 10.11

*(Closes #196 and #172.)*

Jellyfin 12 moved to .NET 10, and a plugin compiled against 10.11 (.NET 9) will not load on it, which is why every action returned **401 / "Unauthorized"** on 12 (#172). Rather than fork the plugin or abandon 10.11 users, this release builds the **same source twice**:

- a **.NET 9** build for Jellyfin **10.11.x** hosts, and
- a **.NET 10** build for Jellyfin **12.x** hosts.

Both are published in the one `manifest.json` under the same plugin, keyed by the Jellyfin version each needs. Jellyfin's own catalog keeps the builds whose target version is at or below your server's and installs the newest, so a 12 server pulls the .NET 10 build, a 10.11 server pulls the .NET 9 build, and neither ever sees the other. **You do not choose a download**: the catalog and auto-update do it for you. If you install manually from the Releases page instead, grab the `-jf12` zip on Jellyfin 12 and the plain zip on 10.11.

Everything was verified end to end on a real Jellyfin 12 server and a Jellyfin 10.11 server: sign-in, refresh persistence, OIDC/SSO, TOTP, email OTP, recovery codes, passkeys, app passwords, admin step-up, the PDF recovery-code export, and the admin dashboard page.

**Related 12 fixes rolled in:**

- **#191** *(camarigor)*: in-app OIDC sign-in on 12 froze on a blank screen. On 12 the router asks for the server connection before the reconnect that 10.11 did first, so the stored credential (which had no resolvable address) left the client pointing at nothing. The sign-in bridge now stores the address it just authenticated against, in the connection mode 12 expects.
- **#193** *(camarigor)*: 12 changed some web routes, so the plugin's setup link and the way it re-enters the setup page needed updating. 12 users get a working way back to the setup page from the avatar menu.
- Completes the header work from v2.5.22 (#174/#180): the plugin's pages and endpoints accept Jellyfin's current `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token` header, which 12 requires once legacy authorization is disabled.

## The admin step-up prompt now appears everywhere it should

*(Closes #198 and #194; helps #189 and #148.)*

The server has gated the sensitive admin actions (creating, editing and deleting OIDC providers, toggling a user's 2FA, "require password setup", and reading the audit log) behind a **step-up** re-authentication since v2.5.6. But some of the admin page's own calls sent those requests with a plain `fetch`, so the server's `403 { stepUpRequired: true }` came back as a bare **"Save failed"** and, for provider **Delete**, nothing happened at all (#198). Adding an identity provider on a step-up-protected server was simply impossible.

- **#198 / #199** *(camarigor)*: the provider form and the shared admin helpers now go through the step-up-aware fetch that Save Settings has used since v2.5.8. When step-up is required you get the prompt; when something else fails you get the server's actual reason instead of a generic message.
- **#194 / #195** *(camarigor)*: the admin step-up modal previously accepted only a typed TOTP code, locking out admins whose second factor is an **emailed code** or a **passkey**. It now offers the emailed code and a passkey alongside TOTP, using the same unified proof the rest of the plugin uses.

If you hit "valid code rejected at step-up" on 10.11 (#189), please retest on this build: the step-up verification and the admin-call routing both changed here.

## GeoIP diagnostics that explain themselves

*(#200, camarigor. Refs #51.)*

Three people reported `GeoIP databases loaded = Fail` with the files in place, and none had a log line to go on, because the loader had nothing to say: it fixed the configured path before trying to open it, a file the process could not see was skipped in silence, and a failed load was never retried until the path changed or Jellyfin restarted. Now the loader keeps the reason, retries, and falls back to an in-memory open, and the Diagnostics tab prints what it saw for **each** database. A bad path no longer reads as a blank "Fail": it says, for example, `not found at /config/geoip/GeoLite2-ASN.mmdb (its directory is not visible to the Jellyfin process; checked as user root)` or `rejected (not absolute)`, so you can actually fix it.

## Upgrade notes

In-place upgrade from any 2.5.x, with no schema or configuration migration. 500 tests pass. Sigstore-signed and SLSA build-provenance attested. Both the 10.11 (.NET 9) and 12 (.NET 10) packages are published for this version; your server selects the right one automatically.

Both are published in the one `manifest.json` under the same plugin, keyed by the Jellyfin version each needs. Jellyfin's own catalog keeps the builds whose target version is at or below your server's and installs the newest, so a 12 server pulls the .NET 10 build, a 10.11 server pulls the .NET 9 build, and neither ever sees the other. **You do not choose a download**: the catalog and auto-update do it for you. If you install manually from the Releases page instead, grab the `-jf12` zip on Jellyfin 12 and the plain zip on 10.11.

Everything was verified end to end on a real Jellyfin 12 server and a Jellyfin 10.11 server: sign-in, refresh persistence, OIDC/SSO, TOTP, email OTP, recovery codes, passkeys, app passwords, admin step-up, the PDF recovery-code export, and the admin dashboard page.

**Related 12 fixes rolled in:**

- **#191** *(camarigor)*: in-app OIDC sign-in on 12 froze on a blank screen. On 12 the router asks for the server connection before the reconnect that 10.11 did first, so the stored credential (which had no resolvable address) left the client pointing at nothing. The sign-in bridge now stores the address it just authenticated against, in the connection mode 12 expects.
- **#193** *(camarigor)*: 12 changed some web routes, so the plugin's setup link and the way it re-enters the setup page needed updating. 12 users get a working way back to the setup page from the avatar menu.
- Completes the header work from v2.5.22 (#174/#180): the plugin's pages and endpoints accept Jellyfin's current `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token` header, which 12 requires once legacy authorization is disabled.

## The admin step-up prompt now appears everywhere it should

*(Closes #198 and #194; helps #189 and #148.)*

The server has gated the sensitive admin actions (creating, editing and deleting OIDC providers, toggling a user's 2FA, "require password setup", and reading the audit log) behind a **step-up** re-authentication since v2.5.6. But some of the admin page's own calls sent those requests with a plain `fetch`, so the server's `403 { stepUpRequired: true }` came back as a bare **"Save failed"** and, for provider **Delete**, nothing happened at all (#198). Adding an identity provider on a step-up-protected server was simply impossible.

- **#198 / #199** *(camarigor)*: the provider form and the shared admin helpers now go through the step-up-aware fetch that Save Settings has used since v2.5.8. When step-up is required you get the prompt; when something else fails you get the server's actual reason instead of a generic message.
- **#194 / #195** *(camarigor)*: the admin step-up modal previously accepted only a typed TOTP code, locking out admins whose second factor is an **emailed code** or a **passkey**. It now offers the emailed code and a passkey alongside TOTP, using the same unified proof the rest of the plugin uses.

If you hit "valid code rejected at step-up" on 10.11 (#189), please retest on this build: the step-up verification and the admin-call routing both changed here.

## GeoIP diagnostics that explain themselves

*(#200, camarigor. Refs #51.)*

Three people reported `GeoIP databases loaded = Fail` with the files in place, and none had a log line to go on, because the loader had nothing to say: it fixed the configured path before trying to open it, a file the process could not see was skipped in silence, and a failed load was never retried until the path changed or Jellyfin restarted. Now the loader keeps the reason, retries, and falls back to an in-memory open, and the Diagnostics tab prints what it saw for **each** database. A bad path no longer reads as a blank "Fail": it says, for example, `not found at /config/geoip/GeoLite2-ASN.mmdb (its directory is not visible to the Jellyfin process; checked as user root)` or `rejected (not absolute)`, so you can actually fix it.

App-password follow-up fixes, self-hosted ntfy delivery, and Keycloak roles / verified-email OIDC linking; in-place upgrade from any 2.5.x, no config changes. FIXED: app-password sessions on native clients such as Symfonium no longer fail on the request right after a successful login ("Can't retrieve Media Info / Version", a 403 "Two-factor authentication required") - this happened when the client's device id on the follow-up request differed from the login request, so the session wasn't recognised as already-verified; the app-password login now marks its session as 2FA-satisfied regardless, and the one-shot is consumed only by its own session so it can't carry over to a later login (#107). Self-hosted ntfy/Gotify/webhooks on a private LAN address (e.g. ntfy.mydomain.com behind a reverse proxy resolving to 192.168.x.x) were silently dropped by the SSRF egress guard ("resolves to private address ... refusing to dispatch"); a new opt-in "Allow notifications to private/LAN addresses" toggle (Settings > Push Notifications, off by default) lets them deliver, while link-local / cloud-metadata addresses (169.254.x, fe80::) stay blocked either way; the ntfy publish URL is also now built as {server}/{topic} (the topic is a path segment, not a header) (#116). OIDC verified-email account linking now works when the IdP encodes email_verified as a boolean, which was previously read as unverified and skipped, causing "no email account match" or a duplicate account (#95). NEW: Keycloak realm/client roles now drive group rules and admin elevation - Keycloak nests roles under realm_access.roles and resource_access.{client}.roles rather than a flat groups/roles claim, so Allowed groups / Admin groups / role-to-library mapping matched nothing; these nested roles are now read from the id_token and /userinfo (request the built-in roles scope and enable "Add to ID token" on the realm-roles mapper) (#95). Translations added for the new setting across all 8 languages. Supports Jellyfin 10.11.9 and newer. Sigstore-signed + SLSA build-provenance attested.

Targeted fix for #95; in-place upgrade from any 2.5.x, no config changes. FIXED: the Setup page no longer breaks behind a reverse proxy that rewrites HTML. If your proxy injects a browser-title/branding script via an nginx sub_filter on the head-closing tag (common for rebranding "Jellyfin" in the browser tab), it was also matching the same tag where it appeared inside one of the Setup page's own inline-JS strings (the recovery-codes print template) - injecting a script-closing tag mid-script, which prematurely ended the page's script element, dumped the rest of the page out as a wall of raw text, and left sections like "Linked Sign-In Methods" stuck on "Loading..." so admins couldn't link a provider (#95, chrisbehectik). The print template now builds every structural tag in split pieces, so no head/title/style/script close tag ever appears as a literal substring for a proxy sub_filter (or another plugin's injection middleware) to latch onto. v2.5.6 - Security and bug-fix release. Critical: closes a stolen-password account-takeover path where a known or guessed client-supplied DeviceId let an attacker skip 2FA via the registered-device / paired-device fallback (the signed trusted-device cookie path was always safe and is unchanged). New BareDeviceIdBypassEnabled config gates the legacy behaviour, default off. Also fixes issue #28 (OIDC redirect_uri built as http behind TLS-terminating reverse proxies - now defaults to https and infers the right scheme from the IdP discovery URL), issue #48 (OIDC sign-in failed when a pre-existing Jellyfin user matched the IdP preferred_username; now links instead of failing), issue #49 (login showed 'incorrect username or password' instead of the 2FA challenge - inject.js race + relative-URL matcher), and issue #50 (email OTP UI said 6-digit but server generated 8; UI now accepts 8 across all bundled languages). Other UX: pending-pairings Deny button now sticks across the next auth retry, Setup page no longer reverts the passkey list to 'Loading' after the i18n pass runs, corrupt user-data JSON now fails closed instead of silently disabling 2FA, runtime CIDR parser rejects out-of-range prefixes, OIDC re-validates cached token/userinfo endpoints per use, ntfy and Gotify now go through the SSRF-pinned client, and passkey labels are sanitized on write and escaped on render. v2.5.5 - Security release. Fixes the OIDC empty-password sign-in path reported via Reddit by Throwaway-3586: newly auto-provisioned OIDC users were created without a password hash, which Jellyfin's default auth provider treats as accepting any password including empty. v2.5.5 sets a 256-bit random password on every OIDC-provisioned user at creation, so the empty-password sign-in is no longer accepted against new accounts. Also fixes the TOTP rotate endpoint (was broken in earlier versions, always rejected the current code) and bundles general security hardening across the auth pipeline (OIDC token algorithm allowlist, discovery-URL validation, recovery-code PBKDF2 bump, email-OTP storage hardening, GeoIP path validation, log scrubbing, race fixes). New optional config 'BlockEmptyPasswordLogin' (default off) extends the empty-password rejection to ALL users at the auth boundary - turn it on if your install doesn't need Jellyfin's kiosk-mode passwordless tile-click sign-in for family / guest accounts. In-place upgrade, no schema changes. One default-on behaviour change: the audit-log endpoint now requires a fresh step-up; lower StepUpLevel if that's inconvenient. 254/254 tests pass. Clean build with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true. Smoke-tested on a live 10.11.10 host: kiosk passwordless tile-click still works, admin 2FA + passkey + Google OIDC + Security Dashboard all functional.

v2.5.4 - Bug fix release. Resolves issue #35 (Snerillinn) - Cloudflare Tunnel and reverse-proxy users were intermittently re-blocked with '[2FA] BLOCKED ... - 2FA not completed' several minutes after a successful passkey/2FA login, locking them out of the UI until a fresh re-auth. Root cause: AuthenticationEventHandler's four legitimate-bypass branches (IsDevicePreVerified, ConsumeQuickConnectPending, userDataPaired, BypassEvaluator.IsBypassed) called ChallengeStore.ApproveToken() to clear the 10-minute BlockToken TTL but did NOT call MarkTokenVerified() to set the 30-day verified flag. Subsequent SessionStarted events fire on every websocket reconnect, new browser tab, and idle-resume - and when those fire from a proxy IP that no longer matches the original bypass condition (very common behind Cloudflare Tunnel where the upstream IP can rotate), BypassEvaluator returns false on the second look, the handler walks the normal challenge path, and re-blocks the same token that was already legitimately approved minutes earlier. Fix: all four bypass branches now ALSO MarkTokenVerified(token), so the 30-day verified flag short-circuits any later SessionStarted re-evaluation regardless of which proxy IP the reconnect arrives from. Bonus: bumps Jellyfin.Controller + Jellyfin.Model SDK targets from 10.11.8 to 10.11.10, with reflection-based adaptation to the 10.11.10 IUserManager.Users (property) -> GetUsers() (method) rename - typeof(IUserManager).GetMethod('GetUsers') preferred at runtime with fallback to the legacy property via string-named GetProperty, so the same DLL still loads on 10.11.0-10.11.9 unchanged. Applied to TwoFactorAuthController.EnumerateAllUsers, StatsService.EnumerateUsers, and SecurityScoreService.EnumerateUsers. Also bumps MailKit 4.16.0 -> 4.17.0 (SMTP fixes upstream) and MaxMind.Db 5.0.0 -> 5.1.0 (GeoLite2 reader perf). 254/254 tests pass on the bumped SDK. Clean build with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true. In-place upgrade - no config changes, no schema changes, no breaking changes for any reverse-proxy or direct-access topology.

v2.5.3 - Follow-up to v2.5.2 (issue #37). Completes the ABI-compatibility fix begun in v2.5.2: the audit that should have run before v2.5.2 missed one more Jellyfin manager property access in the same dashboard endpoint - _sessionManager.Sessions at TwoFactorAuthController:3679 (Overview activeSessions KPI), :2342 (RevokeSession admin endpoint), :2796 (MySessions device enrichment). Same risk class as the _userManager.Users line patched in v2.5.2 - the property's return type changed between Jellyfin 10.11.8 and 10.11.9+, so the IL-emitted callvirt threw System.MissingMethodException at runtime on a 10.11.9+ host. In practice this meant v2.5.2's dashboard fix was incomplete: a 10.11.10 server would throw on the Users line BEFORE v2.5.2 and would throw on the Sessions line AFTER v2.5.2 - the dashboard still returned 'Failed to load dashboard' from a different line. v2.5.3 actually completes the fix. New TwoFactorAuthController.EnumerateSessions() private helper mirrors the existing EnumerateAllUsers() pattern - typeof(ISessionManager).GetProperty(nameof(Sessions)).GetValue() re-binds at runtime against whatever IEnumerable shape the running Jellyfin actually exposes, items downcast to SessionInfo, with try/catch + empty-yield fallback so endpoints degrade gracefully instead of 500-ing. All three callsites routed through it. Full audit of every injected-manager surface (IUserManager, ISessionManager, IDeviceManager, IServerApplicationHost, etc.) verified zero risky direct property accesses remain after v2.5.3 - all other manager calls are method-based with stable signatures across 10.11.x. Plugin now supports Jellyfin 10.11.0 through 10.11.10+ for every code path that depends on injected manager interfaces, and is structurally resistant to future return-type refactors in 10.11.11+ because reflection bypasses static IL binding. 254/254 tests pass. Clean build with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true. In-place upgrade.

v2.5.2 - Bug fix release. Restores the admin Security Dashboard on Jellyfin 10.11.9+ servers. Issue #37: dashboard endpoint and the security-score 'all admins protected' factor both walked _userManager.Users via a statically-bound IL call. Between Jellyfin 10.11.8 (the ABI compiled against) and 10.11.9 the IUserManager.Users return type changed, so the plugin threw System.MissingMethodException at runtime on the newer ABI - surfaced to admins as 'Failed to load dashboard'. Fix routes both broken callsites through the same reflection-based shim already in production at TwoFactorAuthController.EnumerateAllUsers and StatsService.EnumerateUsers - Type.GetProperty(nameof(IUserManager.Users)).GetValue(_userManager) re-binds at runtime against whatever IEnumerable shape the running Jellyfin actually exposes, so it works across 10.11.8 / 10.11.9 / 10.11.10 and any future return-type change that still implements IEnumerable. Patched: TwoFactorAuthController.GetDashboardOverview enrollment-by-role loop, SecurityScoreService.AreAllAdminsProtected (security-score factor #2). Added private EnumerateUsers() helper to SecurityScoreService mirroring the existing pattern. No config / enrollment / OIDC / audit-log changes. 254/254 tests pass. Clean build with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true. In-place upgrade - Jellyfin 10.11.8 users see no behavioural difference, 10.11.9+ users get a working dashboard again.

v2.5.1 - OIDC enhancements + i18n bugfixes + admin UX polish. (1) Per-OIDC-provider ForceHttps toggle: when set, the redirect_uri scheme is pinned to https regardless of forwarded headers. Fixes Cloudflare Tunnel / some Caddy setups that terminate TLS upstream without propagating X-Forwarded-Proto, where the IdP would reject the http:// redirect_uri. Host trust boundary stays intact (only the scheme is overridden) so the existing redirect_uri-poisoning defence against attacker-sent X-Forwarded-Host on untrusted peers is preserved. Wired through model, controller upsert DTO, redirect-URI builder, admin form checkbox, and 8-language i18n. 4 new xUnit tests including the untrusted-host regression case. (2) OIDC Token Exchange (RFC 8693-style): new anonymous endpoint POST /TwoFactorAuth/Oidc/Exchange/{providerId} accepts an id_token from a native client (Swiftfin, Findroid, Tizen apps) that ran its own auth-code+PKCE flow against the IdP with our configured ClientId. Server re-verifies signature, issuer, audience=ClientId, expiry. Nonce check is skipped because the native client used its own nonce - the other id_token protections all still apply. Returns a one-shot bridge token the native client POSTs to /Users/AuthenticateByName, identical to the browser callback flow. Same IP-ban + 20/5min rate limit + per-user IP allowlist gates as /Oidc/Login. OidcService.VerifyIdTokenAsync's expectedNonce is now nullable; extracted FinalizeSignInAsync helper holds the shared post-id_token pipeline (userinfo merge, AMR enforcement, group allowlist, user resolution, SsoLink persistence, AuthenticationProviderId reassignment) so both CompleteAsync and ExchangeIdTokenAsync use the same code path. (3) Language picker selection-state bugfix: renderLanguagePicker rendered synchronously during each page's inline init, but _lang was still 'en' at that point because loadTranslations() is async. The <select> locked to 'English' and never resynced - even hard refresh didn't help because every page-load re-raced. Fix: after rendering, attach _readyPromise.then(syncSelectionFromResolvedLang) so the <select> value updates to _lang once translations resolve. (4) admin-script.js stays [AllowAnonymous]: an earlier internal experiment with [Authorize] broke the script load because same-origin <script src> tags carry COOKIES but NOT the Authorization: MediaBrowser header Jellyfin's auth pipeline checks. Script content is pure JavaScript UI code shipped to every admin browser anyway. (5) 15-second in-memory response cache on /Dashboard/Overview keyed by range (1w/1m/1y): endpoint runs full security-score pipeline (users + audit log + chain verify) + chart build on every hit, so tab switches and range flips would re-pay the bill. With the cache, first load computes, subsequent loads within 15s return instantly. (6) Admin Overview i18n race fix: in non-English locales the bundle fetch finished AFTER renderOverview's innerHTML write, then applyTranslations re-walked [data-i18n-key] containers and overwrote the rendered cards back to translated 'Loading...'. Three-pronged fix: gate the initial renderOverview on window.tfaI18n.ready so the bundle is loaded before the first _tr() call; defensively strip data-i18n-key from factorsGrid + enrollmentBars before setting innerHTML; wire renderLanguagePicker's onChange callback to call renderOverview() so dynamic content re-renders in the new locale. (7) update-badge.yml YAML-quoting fix so OSSF Scorecard's strict parser doesn't trip on the colon inside the commit-message literal. 254/254 tests pass (250 prior + 4 ForceHttps cases). Clean build with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true. In-place upgrade.

v2.4.13 — Bug-fix release. Promotes the v2.4.12.1 diagnostic prerelease to a stable catalog release (identical bytes, version-bumped). Fixes the 'Server not available' regression reported by FsxShader2012 and independently confirmed by Feinstone: v2.4.12's inject.js short-circuit set a sessionStorage.__tfa_pending flag on the post-login page to suppress the Jellyfin Web API barrage during the challenge-page redirect, but the challenge page (a self-contained HTML page that does NOT load inject.js) submitted /TwoFactorAuth/Verify directly without going through the inject.js shim, so the clear-on-Verify-success path never fired. When the user completed 2FA and the challenge page redirected to /web/, inject.js re-mounted on the dashboard, read the still-set flag, and short-circuited every Jellyfin Web API call with a synthetic 403 — surfacing as 'Server not available' because the apiclient interprets persistent non-2xx as the server being unreachable. The failure window depended on browser timing and Jellyfin Web build version which is why some users (including the maintainer's own setup) couldn't reproduce while others hit it every time. Fix: one-line sessionStorage.removeItem('__tfa_pending') at the top of challenge.html's inline script. By the time the user is on the challenge page the flag's job is done; clearing it here means the post-verify navigation back to /web/ is unblocked. inject.js's existing clear-on-Verify-success stays as belt-and-suspenders. Also includes the release.yml 4-part tag truncation fix carried from v2.4.12.1's prerelease — TAG derivation changed from v${VERSION%.*} (strips last .N unconditionally, mangling 4-part prereleases like 2.4.10.1 to v2.4.10) to v${VERSION%.0} (strips trailing .0 only, preserves non-zero build numbers in tags). Verified by v2.4.12.1's artifacts uploading to the correct v2.4.12.1 release instead of clobbering v2.4.12 stable. 181/181 tests pass. In-place upgrade.

v2.4.12 — Bug-fix release bundling three related fixes verified end-to-end on a live Cloudflare → nginx → Jellyfin deployment (passkey + normal + OIDC + email + non-2FA logins, LAN bypass + external XFF resolution + video playback all confirmed green). (1) Closes the LAN-bypass-without-XFF hole reported in the issue #35 follow-up by FsxShader2012: SessionStarted events that fire from websocket reconnects or other non-HTTP-request contexts have no live HttpContext.Request, so v2.4.11's synchronous XFF capture saw null even though the original session came in through the configured reverse proxy. Without a guard the bypass evaluator would fall back to the peer IP (the proxy itself), match the admin's LAN-bypass CIDR, and silently ApproveToken without 2FA. New BypassEvaluator.ShouldRefuseLanBypassWhenXffMissing helper returns true only when TrustForwardedFor is on, forwardedFor is null/empty, AND the peer is inside TrustedProxyCidrs — in that state LAN bypass is refused so the session falls through to the standard 2FA / token-verified / device-paired paths. Direct LAN clients (peer NOT in TrustedProxyCidrs) keep working unchanged. 9 new regression tests cover the trigger case + present-XFF case + direct-LAN-client case + empty-trusted-proxies + empty-remoteIp + multi-CIDR + whitespace-only XFF. (2) Cuts the post-login 401 burst that was tripping SWAG's nginx-unauthorized fail2ban jail, reported in issue #36 by Wibbles42. RequestBlockerMiddleware now returns 403 instead of 401 for the blocked-token-2FA-pending case (semantically more correct since we DO know the caller — they just lack permission until 2FA completes — and crucially nginx-unauthorized's failregex matches only the literal 401 status so 403s are not counted toward brute-force bans). Response body augmented with twoFactorRequired:true so the client-side short-circuit can detect the state from any endpoint, not just the auth-path response. (3) inject.js gains a client-side short-circuit: on the first 401/403 response carrying twoFactorRequired:true, a sessionStorage flag (5-min TTL) is set and subsequent non-allowlisted fetch calls return a synthetic 403 immediately without touching the network. Allowlist mirrors RequestBlockerMiddleware.AlwaysAllowedPaths verbatim so the user can still reach /TwoFactorAuth/Login, /Verify, /Authenticate. Flag clears on successful Verify/Authenticate response. XHR shim only recognises the marker (no short-circuit — synthesising XHR completion events is too brittle for native jellyfin-apiclient consumers); the server-side 401→403 covers any XHR call that races ahead. Combined effect: per-login 401s drop from ~15 to 0, and the residual blocked-token responses are 403s that fail2ban's status-401-only regex never counts. Admins on SWAG / any nginx-unauthorized setup can keep the default maxretry=5 with no constraint on user count behind a shared source IP (Cloudflare, CGNAT, family network). 181/181 tests pass. In-place upgrade.

v2.4.11 — Bug-fix release. (1) Fixes the LAN-bypass-via-reverse-proxy hole reported in the issue #35 follow-up (FsxShader2012). AuthenticationEventHandler.OnSessionStarted called BypassEvaluator.Evaluate with forwardedFor=null, so the bypass evaluator could not walk X-Forwarded-For right-to-left at authentication time. With LAN bypass enabled, every reverse-proxy request whose TCP peer IP (the proxy's address) fell inside a configured LAN-bypass CIDR was treated as a LAN client regardless of the real upstream client IP — silently skipping 2FA for any external user behind a trusted reverse proxy. Fix: inject IHttpContextAccessor into AuthenticationEventHandler and snapshot X-Forwarded-For synchronously inside OnSessionStarted (before the Task.Run handoff, since the background task outlives the HTTP request and reading HttpContext after handoff would race with request completion); plumb the captured header through HandleSessionAsync into BypassEvaluator.Evaluate, which already implemented the SEC-H2 right-to-left walk in PickRealClientIp. The middleware path (TwoFactorEnforcementMiddleware) already read XFF correctly via the same IHttpContextAccessor; only the session-event path was missing it. (2) Promotes v2.4.10.1's diagnostic-build changes into the catalog: TwoFactorEnforcementMiddleware now sets Accept-Encoding: identity on auth-path requests to suppress downstream response compression that would otherwise garble the buffered auth response, and the LooksLikeAuthResponse failure log now surfaces first-8-bytes hex, first-100-chars preview, Content-Encoding header, and Content-Type header so future response-shape mismatches are identifiable in a single round-trip. v2.4.10.1 confirmed working for FsxShader2012's original stuck-on-login symptom (gzip was the culprit); this release bundles those same changes for everyone. 172/172 tests pass. In-place upgrade.

v2.4.10 — Bug-fix release. Fixes issue #35 (FsxShader2012 reported stuck-on-login spinner with 2FA-enabled users). Root cause: TwoFactorEnforcementMiddleware's LooksLikeAuthResponse sniff was case-sensitive (Ordinal) and checked only the PascalCase markers "AccessToken"/"User"/"SessionInfo". Some users' Jellyfin setups (response-wrapping middleware in their stack, or custom JSON naming policy) emit camelCase keys ("accessToken" etc.), which silently failed the substring check. The middleware then passed the auth response straight through with the token intact, RequestBlockerMiddleware blocked subsequent calls token-scoped, and the 2FA challenge UI never rendered. Fix: switched the three substring comparisons from StringComparison.Ordinal to StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase, aligning the sniff with the downstream JsonSerializer.Deserialize which already uses PropertyNameCaseInsensitive=true. The three-key requirement (SEC v2.4 L6) is preserved — third-party admin endpoints returning JSON that mentions just AccessToken+User still won't get pulled into the 2FA flow. The v2.4.9 diagnostic Info log is retained so any future stranger response shape (snake_case, wrapped JSON, etc.) surfaces immediately. Note: v2.4.9 was a diagnostic-only pre-release (not in this catalog) used to gather the data that led to this fix. 172/172 tests pass (6 new LooksLikeAuthResponseTests pinning PascalCase, camelCase, mixed-case, missing-key, oversized, and HTML cases). In-place upgrade.

v2.4.8 — Bug-fix release. Two real defects reported in issue #29 (Authelia + Gmail SMTP setup). (1) SMTP test email over port 465 silently failed because System.Net.Mail.SmtpClient.EnableSsl=true triggers STARTTLS rather than Implicit TLS — port 465 expects a TLS handshake BEFORE any SMTP commands. Fix: migrated to MailKit. New PickSocketOptions helper maps port 465 → SslOnConnect, port 587 → StartTls, other ports + UseSsl=true → StartTlsWhenAvailable. (2) OIDC sign-in via Authelia rejected users as 'not part of allowed groups' even when scopes included groups. Root cause: the plugin only read claims from the id_token JWT, but Authelia (default config), Keycloak (most realms), and Authentik emit groups/email/email_verified only at the /userinfo endpoint. Fix: after id_token verification, the plugin now fetches /userinfo with the access_token and merges any groups, roles, email, email_verified, and username claims before the AllowedGroups check and ResolveUserAsync. Validated end-to-end on a real Authelia 4.39 instance (same IdP family as the reporter) plus a real Gmail smtp.gmail.com:465 send. Ships MailKit + MimeKit + BouncyCastle.Cryptography in the fat package (~7.2MB total). 166/166 tests pass (5 new SMTP socket-option tests, 6 new userinfo extraction tests). In-place upgrade.

v2.4.7 — Bug-fix release. Fixes the OIDC redirect_uri http:// bug reported in issue #28 (Kanidm + cloudflared). Root cause: BuildRedirectUri's proxy-header check required BOTH X-Forwarded-Proto AND X-Forwarded-Host to be present before honoring either. Reverse-proxy setups that only emit X-Forwarded-Proto (cloudflared, many nginx configs, some Caddy setups) fell through to Request.Scheme which is 'http' when TLS terminates upstream; the IdP correctly rejected per the OAuth spec exact-match comparison. Fix: each forwarded header is now evaluated independently — X-Forwarded-Proto honored regardless of X-Forwarded-Host's presence, and vice versa. The proxyTrusted gate (peer must be in TrustedProxyCidrs) is unchanged for BOTH header checks, so attackers connecting directly still cannot inject either header. The URL-construction logic was extracted to a pure static helper OidcRedirectUriBuilder so it's testable without HttpContext mocking, and 5 regression tests were added covering happy path, the issue #28 fix, and two security-boundary regressions (untrusted-peer Proto + Host spoofing must remain ignored). 155/155 tests pass. In-place upgrade.

v2.4.6 — Bug-fix release. Fixes the 'logged out every couple of minutes' loop reported in issue #27. Root cause: AuthenticationEventHandler subscribes to ISessionManager.SessionStarted, which fires not only on initial login but also on websocket reconnects, new tabs, idle-resume, and reverse-proxy WS drops (Traefik, Caddy, nginx). Once the 2-minute pre-verify window expired, the handler's failsafe BlockToken re-blocked the user's active access token; RequestBlockerMiddleware then 401'd every subsequent request, the client retried, a new SessionStarted fired, repeat. Fix: ChallengeStore now tracks tokens that have completed 2FA at least once in this process lifetime (30-day TTL, capped + swept). AuthenticationEventHandler skips the failsafe block and the session-end for verified tokens, treating those SessionStarted events as reconnects (audit log Method='reconnect'). The failsafe still fires for genuinely unverified tokens. Secondary fix: Jellyfin 10.11.9 changed IUserManager.Users's return type in a non-ABI-compatible way; StatsService.ComputeAsync and the AdminForceLogout 'last admin' guard now use reflection-based enumeration so they no longer throw MissingMethodException on 10.11.9 hosts. In-place upgrade.

v2.4.0 — Security hardening, per-role policy, breach-password check, and 'Where am I signed in?'. HIBP (opt-in): on sign-in, the first 5 hex chars of SHA-1(password) are sent to api.pwnedpasswords.com (k-anonymity); a breach hit writes an audit entry and warning log but never blocks sign-in; fails open on outage.
